- **Theorem** `ERealStieltjes.measure_add`
  `(f : ERealStieltjes) (g : ERealStieltjes) : (f + g).measure = (f.measure + g.measure).restrict {x | ↑(f + g) x ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∀ y < x, ↑(f + g) y ≠ ⊤}`
  — The measure of a sum of `ERealStieltjes` functions. `(f + g) x` is `⊤` as soon as `f x` or `g x` is `⊤`, and `⊥` if one of them is `⊥` and none is `⊤`. The measure `(f + g).measure` sees only the region where `f + g` is finite, together with the point at which it jumps to `⊤`, and it agrees with `f.measure + g.measure` there.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>∀ (f g : ERealStieltjes), (f + g).measure = (f.measure + g.measure).restrict {x | ↑(f + g) x ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∀ y &lt; x, ↑(f + g) y ≠ ⊤}</code></details>

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.DivFunction.rightDerivStieltjes`
  `(f : DivFunction) : ERealStieltjes`
  — The right derivative of `f`, as a monotone right-continuous function `ℝ → EReal`: it is `⊥` below `f.xmin`, `⊤` from `f.xmax` on, and in between it is the right limit of the right derivative of `f.realFun` (which is that right derivative itself, except possibly at `f.xmin` where the right derivative of `f.realFun` can be `-∞`).
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>DivFunction → ERealStieltjes</code></details>

- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.integrable_f_rnDeriv_compProd_iff`
  `[MeasurableSpace.CountableOrCountablyGenerated α β] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] [IsFiniteKernel κ] [IsFiniteKernel η] (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) (h_cvx : ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ici 0) f) : Integrable (fun x => f ((μ.compProd κ).rnDeriv (ν.compProd η) x).toReal) (ν.compProd η) ↔ (∀ᵐ (a : α) ∂ν, Integrable (fun x => f (μ.rnDeriv ν a * (κ a).rnDeriv (η a) x).toReal) (η a)) ∧ Integrable (fun a => ∫ (b : β), f (μ.rnDeriv ν a * (κ a).rnDeriv (η a) b).toReal ∂η a) ν`
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} {μ ν : Measure α} {κ η : Kernel α β} {f : ℝ → ℝ} [MeasurableSpace.CountableOrCountablyGenerated α β] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] [IsFiniteKernel κ] [IsFiniteKernel η], StronglyMeasurable f → ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ici 0) f → (Integrable (fun x =&gt; f ((μ.compProd κ).rnDeriv (ν.compProd η) x).toReal) (ν.compProd η) ↔ (∀ᵐ (a : α) ∂ν, Integrable (fun x =&gt; f (μ.rnDeriv ν a * (κ a).rnDeriv (η a) x).toReal) (η a)) ∧ Integrable (fun a =&gt; ∫ (b : β), f (μ.rnDeriv ν a * (κ a).rnDeriv (η a) b).toReal ∂η a) ν)</code></details>

  `(ha_ne : a ≠ 1) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] [NeZero μ] [NeZero ν] : ∫ (x : α), (μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal ^ a ∂ν = (μ Set.univ).toReal ^ a * (ν Set.univ).toReal ^ (1 - a) * ∫ (x : α), (((μ Set.univ)⁻¹ • μ).rnDeriv ((ν Set.univ)⁻¹ • ν) x).toReal ^ a ∂(ν Set.univ)⁻¹ • ν`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.hellingerFun`
  `(a : ℝ) (_ : ℝ) : ℝ`
  — Hellinger function, defined as `x ↦ (a - 1)⁻¹ * (x ^ a - 1)` for `a ∈ (0, 1) ∪ (1, + ∞)`. At `0` the function is obtained by contiuity and is the indicator function of `{0}`. At `1` it is defined as `x ↦ x * log x`, because in this way we obtain that the Hellinger divergence at `1` conincides with the KL divergence, which is natural for continuity reasons.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>ℝ → ℝ → ℝ</code></details>
- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.integrable_hellingerFun_iff_integrable_rpow`

## 22. `TestingLowerBounds.Divergences.Hellinger.HellingerDivFun`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.hellingerDivFun`
  `(a : ℝ) : DivFunction`
  — The divergence function of the Hellinger divergence of order `a`: for `0 < a`, it is the `DivFunction` obtained from `hellingerFun a` (which is `klFun` for `a = 1`). For `a ≤ 0` it is `0`: `hellingerFun a` is not convex for `a < 0`, and for `a = 0` the value of a `DivFunction` at `0` is determined by continuity, so the indicator of `{0}` cannot be used.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>ℝ → DivFunction</code></details>
- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.derivAtTop_hellingerDivFun`
  `(hellingerDivFun a).derivAtTop = if a ≤ 0 then 0 else if a < 1 then ENNReal.ofReal (a * (1 - a)⁻¹) else ⊤`
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>∀ {a : ℝ}, (hellingerDivFun a).derivAtTop = if a ≤ 0 then 0 else if a &lt; 1 then ENNReal.ofReal (a * (1 - a)⁻¹) else ⊤</code></details>

## 23. `TestingLowerBounds.Divergences.Hellinger.Hellinger`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.hellingerDiv`
  `(a : ℝ) (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure α) : ENNReal`
  — Hellinger divergence of order `a`, the f-divergence for the function `hellingerDivFun a`. For `a = 1` the Hellinger divergence coincides with the Kullback-Leibler divergence. For `a ≤ 0` the divergence function is `0`, hence `hellingerDiv a μ ν = 0`. In particular `hellingerDiv 0 μ ν = 0`: the value `ν {x | (∂μ/∂ν) x = 0}` that is sometimes used as Hellinger divergence of order `0` in the literature is not the f-divergence of a `DivFunction`, since such a function has to be continuous at `0`. The Rényi divergence of order `0` is defined separately (see `renyiDiv`).
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{α : Type u_1} → {mα : MeasurableSpace α} → ℝ → Measure α → Measure α → ENNReal</code></details>

## 25. `TestingLowerBounds.Divergences.Renyi.Renyi`

- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.avgMass`
  `(a : ℝ) (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure α) : ℝ`
  — Weighted average `(1 - a) * ν univ + a * μ univ` of the masses of `μ` and `ν`, as a real number.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{α : Type u_1} → {mα : MeasurableSpace α} → ℝ → Measure α → Measure α → ℝ</code></details>
- **Definition** `ProbabilityTheory.renyiDiv`
  `(a : ℝ) (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure α) : ENNReal`
  — Rényi divergence of order `a` between finite measures. It is the Rényi divergence of the normalized measures `(μ univ)⁻¹ • μ` and `(ν univ)⁻¹ • ν` (see `renyiDiv_smul_left` and `renyiDiv_smul_right`): for `a ∉ {0, 1}`, `Rₐ(μ, ν) = (a - 1)⁻¹ * (log (∫ x, ((∂μ/∂ν) x) ^ a ∂ν) - log (μ(univ) ^ a * ν(univ) ^ (1 - a)))`, which is the usual `(a - 1)⁻¹ * log (∫ x, ((∂μ/∂ν) x) ^ a ∂ν)` for probability measures. The integral is written as `(1 - a) * ν(univ) + a * μ(univ) + (a - 1) * Hₐ(μ, ν)` in terms of the Hellinger divergence, which makes the Rényi divergence a monotone function of the Hellinger divergence for fixed masses. For `a = 1` it is the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the normalized measures and for `a = 0` it is `- log (ν {∂μ/∂ν > 0} / ν(univ))`. We use ENNReal.log instead of Real.log, because it is monotone on `ℝ≥0∞`, while the real log is monotone only on `(0, ∞)` (`Real.log 0 = 0`). This allows us to transfer inequalities from the Hellinger divergence to the Rényi divergence.
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>{α : Type u_1} → {mα : MeasurableSpace α} → ℝ → Measure α → Measure α → ENNReal</code></details>
- **Theorem** `ProbabilityTheory.renyiDiv_of_lt_one`
  `[IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (ha_pos : 0 < a) (ha_lt : a < 1) : renyiDiv a μ ν = if μ.MutuallySingular ν then ⊤ else ENNReal.ofReal ((a - 1)⁻¹ * (Real.log (∫ (x : α), (μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal ^ a ∂ν) - (a * Real.log (μ Set.univ).toReal + (1 - a) * Real.log (ν Set.univ).toReal)))`
  <details><summary>Full Lean statement</summary><code>∀ {α : Type u_1} {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {μ ν : Measure α} {a : ℝ} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν], 0 &lt; a → a &lt; 1 → renyiDiv a μ ν = if μ.MutuallySingular ν then ⊤ else ENNReal.ofReal ((a - 1)⁻¹ * (Real.log (∫ (x : α), (μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal ^ a ∂ν) - (a * Real.log (μ Set.univ).toReal + (1 - a) * Real.log (ν Set.univ).toReal)))</code></details>

  `[IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : fDiv f μ ν + ENNReal.ofReal (rightDeriv f.realFun 1) * ν Set.univ = ∫⁻ (x : ℝ), fDiv (statInfoDivFun 1 x) μ ν ∂f.curvatureMeasureReal + ENNReal.ofReal (rightDeriv f.realFun 1) * μ Set.univ`
  — Integral representation of `fDiv f μ ν` in terms of the f-divergences of the `statInfoDivFun 1 x` and the curvature measure of `f`.
